selection: All nineteen newly assigned full bodies, one fully read prior-support brief, all eight later embedding lessons, seven complete original-to-later diffs, one whole-byte-identical original reuse, and sixteen fresh whole native views.

sourceFirstUnits.requirement: Conditioning defines a group and does not establish causation; the conditional-probability ratio requires a nonzero conditioning probability.
The observation unit, person-time rate and incomplete-follow-up risk question are distinct.
The same five observed responses appear among 20 enrolled, 14 treated and 10 scan-evaluable people, giving 25%, approximately 35.7% and 50%.
Four treated people without evaluable scans and six untreated people are separate groups with no supplied response outcome.
Five evaluable scans did not meet the response rule; all rows retain the same five responding people.
Observed responder fractions do not establish a protocol analysis set or silently recode unknown outcomes as confirmed nonresponse.
The three sets are nested; the chart uses an absolute common count scale and equal-sized person slots rather than normalized percentage bars.
Changing the counted set is a fictional denominator comparison, not response improvement over time, a RECIST rule or clinical benefit.
The separate complete-cohort brain-involvement fractions are 5/20=25% and 5/100=5%; the 8/20 scan exercise gives 40% without resolving other outcomes.

In the same fictional course, death stays at year 6 while detection moves from year 4 to year 3; recorded survival changes from two to three years.
The additional recorded year moves only the measurement origin and supplies no evidence of longer life or benefit from earlier treatment.
The aligned linear time scales and symbolic stopwatch illustrate an interval rather than a time-of-day reading.
Lead-time bias, length bias and overdiagnosis are distinct; screening magnitudes do not automatically transfer to molecular monitoring.
A strategy comparison needs a common origin, intended actions, outcomes and harms, including all assigned people rather than detectable signals alone.
A specific surveillance/intervention feasibility result does not establish a beneficial window for every earlier signal; the later surveillance cross-reference has its own historical scope.
